ops.title: container-hermes egress pf (2e): design, ordering, and posture options
ops.body:
Design record for `scripts/host/container-pf.sh` — the egress pf anchor for the container-native hermes agent (Architecture B, plan z-4-virtual-generic-lampson). Authored 2026-07-17; live test GATED (unproven — the prototype's B2 egress-enforcement leg never ran). Supersedes nothing; complements [[host-pf.sh]]'s fleet anchor.

## What the container's egress actually is (empirical — prototype verdict note 4656afb)

The hermes agent runs as an apple/container OCI container on the DEFAULT vmnet-NAT network, subnet **192.168.72.0/24** (config.toml override; avoids the fleet's 192.168.64.0/24). That is a **different host bridge** than host-pf.sh guards, so host-pf's `on <fleet-bridge>` rules never see container traffic — without a dedicated anchor the container's egress is unpoliced.

apple/container's default network was measured to ALREADY isolate the container from: the fleet (vmnet 64.x AND tailnet 100.x), the host gateway/LAN, and IPv6. **Only IPv4 TCP was tested.** The ONE real leak: a default-NAT container reaches the **host's own services** (it NATs through the host) — rapid-mlx :8000, mlx-audio :8765 — plus the open internet.

Decisive config fact (nixos/hermes.nix): the agent addresses EVERYTHING as `metal:*` over its own in-container WireGuard tun — model plane `metal:8000/8317`, STT `metal:8765`, cooperative HTTPS_PROXY `metal:14322` — and makes **zero direct cleartext internet connections** (every non-metal host, incl. openai/exa/honcho, routes through the proxy). So blocking the container from `self` + all private space costs the agent nothing; its only legitimate cleartext egress on this bridge is its own tailscaled transport (WG/disco UDP + DERP/control 443 + DNS).

## The anchor: com.apple/000.yclaw.container

Child of the stock pf.conf `anchor "com.apple/*"` wildcard (evaluated from the first targeted load). Every rule is `in quick on <bridge>` (ingress, before routing) so a NET_ADMIN guest can't slip a verdict by forging a source; a terminal `block drop from any to any` makes the anchor **TOTAL for its bridge**. Bridge interface resolved per tick by the address carrying 192.168.72.1 (drifts across restarts, like Tart's).

### Two load-bearing subtleties (both found during authoring; codex-reviewed)

1. **Ordering vs host-pf — forged-source bypass.** host-pf's model-port pass (`pass in quick proto tcp from {metal} to any port <ports>`, host-pf.sh ~line 144) is NOT interface-scoped. A container forging `src=metal` → `host:8000` on ITS bridge would match that pass. Fix: name this anchor `000.yclaw.container`, which sorts ALPHABETICALLY BEFORE `000.yclaw.host` under the wildcard, and make it total — so host-pf never adjudicates a packet on the container bridge. Interface-scoping keeps the two disjoint, so host-pf's own 64.x traffic is unaffected by evaluating this first.
2. **`to any` self-leak.** The tier-2 egress passes use `to any`, which includes host addresses. The `block ... to self` + private-space blocks MUST precede them, or `pass tcp from CNET to any port 443` etc. would readmit the host on the permitted ports (re-opening the rapid-mlx leak). Order: gateway DNS/DHCP carve-out → tier-1 deny (self/private/mcast/bcast) → tier-2 passes → terminal deny.

## Ruleset shape (moderate posture, the shipped default)

```
pass out quick on IF to CNET keep state                       # host->container replies (parity w/ host-pf)
pass in  quick on IF proto udp from CNET to CGW port {53,67,68}  # only permitted self access: gw DNS/DHCP
pass in  quick on IF proto tcp from CNET to CGW port 53
pass in  quick on IF proto udp from 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255 port 67  # DHCP DISCOVER pre-lease
block drop in quick on IF from any to self                    # tier-1 lateral-movement deny (from any = forged too)
block drop in quick on IF inet  from any to 224.0.0.0/4
block drop in quick on IF from any to 255.255.255.255
block drop in quick on IF from any to CBCAST
block drop in quick on IF inet6 from any to ff00::/8
block drop in quick on IF inet  from any to {10/8,172.16/12,192.168/16,169.254/16,100.64/10}
block drop in quick on IF inet6 from any to {fc00::/7,fe80::/10}
pass in  quick on IF proto udp from CNET to any port 53       # tier-2: tailscaled transport to PUBLIC only
pass in  quick on IF proto tcp from CNET to any port 53
pass in  quick on IF proto udp from CNET to any               # WG/disco (varying ports)
pass in  quick on IF proto tcp from CNET to any port 443      # DERP + control
block drop in quick on IF from any to any                     # terminal default-deny (forged + any other port)
```

Loaded via `install_pf_anchor --wire-load-only --enable` (pf.sh); never `pfctl -f /etc/pf.conf`. Refreshed by a root LaunchDaemon `com.yclaw.container-pf-refresh` (RunAtLoad + KeepAlive sleep-loop; StartInterval is dead on Tahoe), backoff-until-first-tick because the bridge doesn't exist until container-hermes.sh brings the apiserver/network up.

## tier-2 posture options (the user decision)

The agent makes NO direct cleartext internet connections, so tier-2 only ever fences a *compromised* agent's raw egress.
- **Permissive (A):** tier-1 only; public egress default-passes. Relies entirely on the no-secrets + proxy structural model. Simplest, most robust.
- **Moderate (B) — shipped default:** tier-1 + permit only {DNS, WG UDP, 443} to public + terminal deny. Blocks arbitrary ports; a compromised agent can still exfil over 443. Near-zero breakage; no IP-list maintenance.
- **Strict (C):** like B but pins the passes to Tailscale's published control+DERP CIDRs + terminal deny. The only posture that meaningfully contains a compromised agent (forces pivots through the tailnet/proxy). FRAGILE: DERP CIDR drift breaks the tailnet; needs a refresh source; live-test-gated + unproven. Recommended as a follow-up hardening AFTER the base migration is proven, not layered onto an unproven stack.

## Residual / open
- Live test never run (prototype B2 deferred). The bridge-timing question (does the 192.168.72.1 bridge exist at `container system start`, or only at first `container run`?) governs the brief unprotected window between container-up and the first container-pf tick — observe during Phase 3, then consider gating `container run` on the pf marker (do NOT hard-couple if it risks a deadlock).
- Only IPv4 TCP was prototype-tested; this anchor is proto-agnostic (`from any` blocks) to cover the untested UDP/mDNS/full-port surface.
